pages.text: All the snow in the yard had melted. Grandma gave Yuki a bag of flower seeds. Momo pressed a nose to the bag and sniffed.
"I'll make my flower garden here." Yuki drew a line with a toe at one side of the yard.
Yuki poked the ground with a stick. It would not go in. "Why can't I dig? Is it stone?"
Momo scraped beneath the wall with front paws. Dark soil puffed up. "Go away, Momo. That's not my flower garden."
Yuki threw down the stick. "I'll just scatter them here." Seeds spilled over the hard soil.
Spring rain fell that night. Yuki peered into the yard through the door. "It's raining!"
In the morning, Yuki went outside. Not a seed remained. "Where did they all go?"
Grandma put a handful of soil into Yuki's hand. It was cold and hard. "It's like stone."
A few days later, Yuki pushed a finger into the ground. "It's soft now!" Yuki put one seed in each hole and covered it with soil.
Little green dots sprouted from the earth. Yuki crouched beside them and counted each one.
